statement: For every nonempty alpha in S_a and beta in S_b, let j(p)=(m^4+2m^3+m^2+4m+4)/2-g_2(p) for m=|p|, and let T(alpha), H(beta) indicate a decreasing last, respectively first, sum-indecomposable component, including singletons. Then j(alpha direct-sum beta)=j(alpha)+j(beta)+T(alpha)H(beta). Internal Ray--West good gaps restrict exactly to the summands and the join is good exactly when T(alpha)H(beta)=1. Value complementation gives the skew-sum rule with increasing skew components. Consequently j on every separable permutation equals the sum over maximal decomposition-tree nodes of adjacent decreasing-child pairs at sum nodes and adjacent increasing-child pairs at skew nodes. Among sum-decomposable permutations j(p)=|p|-1 if and only if p is layered; among skew-decomposable permutations equality holds if and only if p is colayered. No full-scope formula or equality classification is claimed for permutations indecomposable in both senses.
contribution: A proposed exact composition law for arbitrary summands, with an intrinsic computable statistic on all separable permutations and equality classification on all sum/skew-decomposable permutations. The proof repairs a false coordinate-only clipping step by re-pairing inserted points. It builds on the known Ray--West active-track count; no equivalent composition law was found in the bounded primary-source comparison, including Shar's prior repeated-sum work. Original Problem 3.7 remains unresolved; correctness and contribution await a fresh referee.
